reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's care and desire for Israel's wellbeing. In 1 Samuel 9:16, God tells Samuel: 'I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be prince over my people Israel. He shall save my people from the hand of the Philistines; for I have seen the affliction of my people, because their cry has come to me.' This passage reveals that Yahweh has observed the people's suffering, heard their cry, and is actively intervening by providing a deliverer (Saul) to save them from oppression. Furthermore, in 1 Samuel 12:7-8, Samuel recounts how Yahweh brought Israel up from Egypt and delivered them from the hand of all kingdoms that oppressed them, establishing a pattern of divine care and protection. The selection and anointing of Saul as king is framed as a concrete act of salvation in response to the people's distress.
